use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: To determine whether two tracks, which may have been reported by different sensors or systems, represent the same physical object.

goal.raw_text: To determine whether two tracks, which may have been reported by different sensors or systems, represent the same physical object.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU receives track data from multiple sources which may contain dual designations for the same physical object.
The C2 JU identifies two tracks that are candidates for correlation based on proximity in time and space.

The C2 JU performs an automatic correlation test by comparing the positional data of the two tracks against established criteria, including position tolerance, velocity difference, and altitude difference.
If the tracks meet all the automatic correlation criteria, the system declares them correlated and assigns a common Track Number to both, resolving the dual designation.
If the tracks fail the automatic correlation test but are still suspected to be the same object, the C2 JU may initiate a manual correlation process.
Upon successful manual correlation, the C2 JU formally associates the tracks, assigning a single Track Number and updating the track information accordingly.

If a track being considered for correlation has an 'Unconfirmed' status (e.g., from a new sensor report), it may be held in a tentative state until its status becomes 'Confirmed' before proceeding with automatic or manual correlation.

If the initial automatic correlation test fails, but the tracks are still suspected to be the same object, the C2 JU can adjust the correlation criteria (e.g., increase position tolerance) and re-run the test before resorting to full manual correlation.

During a manual correlation attempt, if the operator determines the tracks do not represent the same object, the process is terminated, and the tracks remain separate with their original designations.

If a reverse correlation request is received from another unit after a local correlation has been established, the local unit must evaluate the request. If accepted, it will de-correlate the local tracks and transmit a message confirming the de-correlation to allow the remote unit's correlation to proceed.

If the automatic correlation test fails and manual correlation is not initiated or also fails, the tracks remain uncorrelated with their original designations. The system continues to track them as separate entities.

If a track involved in a correlation attempt is dropped (e.g., due to loss of sensor contact) before the process is complete, the correlation attempt is terminated. If a correlation had already been established, the remaining track retains its correlated status until it is also dropped or de-correlated by other means.

If conflicting correlation requests are received from multiple external units regarding the same set of local tracks, the local unit must apply conflict resolution rules (e.g., based on priority of the requesting unit) to determine which request to honor, potentially rejecting others.

If an error occurs during the data exchange required for correlation (e.g., a corrupted message), the specific correlation attempt for those tracks is aborted. The system may log the error and await retransmission of valid data before retrying.
The two tracks are assigned a single, common Track Number.
The track data from both original reports is merged or associated under the new common Track Number.
The dual designation for the physical object is resolved within the C2 JU's system.
If the correlation was performed automatically, the tracks are marked as correlated in the system database.
If the correlation was performed manually, an operator has explicitly confirmed the association, and the tracks are updated accordingly.
Subsequent surveillance reports for the object will be associated with the new, single Track Number.
